findings.title: First occurrence of every customer raises TypeError
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 2: “It works when a customer appears for the first time.” This also defeats criteria 1, 3, and 4.
findings.trigger: Any well-formed CSV containing at least one data row reaches a customer not yet present in `totals`.
findings.consequence: `totals.get(cust)` returns `None`, so adding the row's float amount raises `TypeError`; the function returns no aggregation result.
findings.evidence: Line 11: `totals[cust] = totals.get(cust) + float(row["amount"])` omits a numeric default such as `0` from `dict.get`.

reasoning: The supplied SHA-256 matches the artifact record. Tracing the first valid data row shows an unconditional exception before any customer can be inserted, so the implementation cannot satisfy the stated criteria and the defect meets the blocker threshold.
